title: Name Pecoraro and the nickname Peck
summary: Pecora explains his surname, how Johnny Vittroy began calling him Peck, and why he kept Santo in New Orleans after Chicago and California.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Can we get your name now?
I don't know your real full name. I don't know what J is for. Joseph. Joseph, okay.

So, what is your real name? My last name is Pecoraro, but I cut it down to Pecoraro. You just called yourself Santa Pecoraro? Yes, and it's a funny thing, then it was about 19, oh, let me see, 19, 20, around 20, Johnny Vittroy started calling me Peck instead of Pecoraro, see? And then when I went to Chicago, they used to make my check out, Peck Pecoraro instead of going to be a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a little bit of a little bit. So, I stayed in Chicago 15 years, and when I went to California, everybody called me Peck, you know, they knew me from playing the theater there. Am I talking over the telephone? It's working fine. Yeah. So, then I got out there, and, well, I was out in California for about 12 years, and I came back to New Orleans. My mother got crippled, that's why I got back to New Orleans. But my Dave Rose and a bunch of musicians that I worked with in California, they see my picture out there, it says, Santo. They said, well, that's Peck, that's not Santo. I said, where the hell did he get that name? So, Dave looked in the front door, I said, hey, Dave, come in, see? He says, why the hell did you change the name to Santo? See, he says, I said, you're right, everybody, but I said, down in New Orleans, everybody knows me, you know, Santo. So, I just kept the name Santo.
